The Taliban authorities support the TTP, according to the UN; the Taliban deny harbouring terrorist groups and moved about 2,000 TTP members inland. Contested: the Taliban publicly deny it.1

Boko Haram (JAS) and ISWAP are rival splinters of the original Boko Haram.61

Syrian security forces raid Islamic State cells; two officers and five Islamic State members died in Rankous on 22 October 2026.15

Pakistan's ISI is reported to have put military officers in charge of coordinating LeT, JeM and Hizbul Mujahideen operations. Single Indian news-agency report.97

incidents.html: US troops leave Iraq; Kata'ib Hezbollah says it has agreed no disarmament deal and 'the resistance has won this round'.47
Suspected Boko Haram fighters kill 15 or more farmers and firewood gatherers; three are missing. Reuters says 'suspected Islamists'; AP says 15 dead.62,99

incidents.place: Rask and Iranshahr area, Sistan and Baluchestan, Iran
incidents.html: The Baluch coalition claims five attacks on Iranian security forces in seven days, including a mine and gunfire attack on a Guards vehicle at Rudmahi that killed five. Claims by the coalition; Iranian figures for losses are lower.76

A motorcycle bomb targets a Taliban intelligence official; ISKP claims it and the National Resistance Front also claims it. Contested: two competing claims; neither authenticated; Afghan authorities have not confirmed.100,101

incidents.place: Mokha and Bab el-Mandeb area, Yemen
incidents.html: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they retook areas around the Bab el-Mandeb strait; the Houthis deny losing ground. Contested: government claim versus Houthi denial.37,102

Islamic State Mozambique fighters attack Christians at Ngangolo; on 10 October two Christians are beheaded near Muangaza, Mocímboa da Praia. Source for the two named incidents is a weak tracker (trackingterrorism.org); the ReliefWeb monitor confirms a wave of violence in September–October only.25,103,104

Mali's army, backed by Africa Corps (Russian state-run force), retakes Kidal after JNIM and FLA forces withdraw; the Soufan Center calls the gain politically important but strategically limited. Kidal coordinates are the town centre.10
JNIM reportedly seizes army bases and posts at Tougouri, Gomboro and Diabiga. Single graded aggregator that relays party claims; not independently confirmed.105,106

Suspected Lakurawa fighters on more than 100 motorcycles attack a forward operating base at Maiyama, which troops repel; a day later they kill two soldiers and a Chinese worker on the Sokoto-Badagry highway project. Police and the military attribute it to suspected Lakurawa fighters; no claim reported.23

incidents.place: Tessit and Oudalan, Mali/Burkina Faso border
incidents.html: JNIM and the Islamic State Sahel Province fight near Tessit and Oudalan; ISSP claims 400+ JNIM dead, unverified. Exact date not established; toll unverified.107,10

incidents.place: King Khalid International Airport, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
incidents.html: A Houthi missile hits the domestic terminal; 12 killed and about 300 wounded; the Houthis claim it. A follow-up strike the next day reportedly killed one more person (NPR). Airport coordinates assigned by the researcher.34,108

Pakistan says TTP-linked fighters tried to cross from Afghanistan, Afghan Taliban posts opened fire, and 12 militants and Afghan personnel died; one Pakistani soldier killed. Pakistani military account; Afghan authorities had not responded.55

Suspected ISWAP fighters storm a military base; 15 soldiers and five civilian militia members reported killed, vehicles burned, troops withdraw toward Monguno. First reports gave 'more than 10 soldiers and four civilians'.20,19,109

incidents.place: Sultan Mastura, Maguindanao del Norte, Philippines
incidents.html: Police and soldiers kill a Dawlah Islamiyah sub-leader and three followers serving arrest warrants. Faction not named in the report.75

incidents.place: Bakaheku mining sites, Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
incidents.html: An attack attributed to the ADF on three mining sites kills 10 people. Attribution is by local reporters.24
Islamic State Sahel Province fighters attack civilian camps; at least 48 are killed (Mali's army later reports 54 bodies). Coordinates are the nearest town, about 50 km away.22,110,111

Two Western hostages (one Swiss, one Austrian) held in Niger for 18 and 21 months are freed and flown to Benghazi. Holder reported as Islamic State Sahel Province; the release terms are not public.112
Syrian forces raid a suspected Islamic State cell; two officers and five cell members killed, six arrested.15

Al-Shabaab ambushes Somali troops; at least 20 soldiers killed per a survivor, dozens per other reports; the army claims about 75 militants killed. Tolls differ widely across sources; al-Shabaab claims 321.13

incidents.place: Daraa and Suwayda countryside, southern Syria
incidents.html: Jordan strikes what it calls Islamic State hideouts in southern Syria after the 23 October Karak church shooting that killed nine; Jordan says more than 20 militants died, Syria says seven civilians died and denies coordinating. Contested: Jordan links the church attackers to Islamic State in Syria, but Jordanian officials also say the three arrested Jordanians acted alone, and no group claim is confirmed by Reuters.16,113
A military-escorted convoy of 1,107 fuel tankers reaches Bamako, the fourth convoy in October; JNIM's fuel blockade of the capital runs since April 2026.114,115

incidents.place: Dharin and Qurac, Cal Miskaad mountains, Bari, Somalia
incidents.html: Puntland forces fight Islamic State in the heaviest clash of their offensive; Puntland says 57 foreign fighters and 15 soldiers died; the UAE flies a supporting drone strike. Toll is a Puntland claim that VOA could not verify; coordinates are an approximate mountain area.27,116

incidents.place: Southern Lebanon (near Shoukin, Mayfadoun and Qantara)
incidents.html: Israeli drone and air strikes continue in southern Lebanon despite the June ceasefire framework; Hezbollah leader Qassem rejects disarmament. Coordinates are approximate for the Nabatieh area. Reports of Hezbollah rebuilding drone capability come from Lebanese sources cited by Times of Israel.31,29

The Houthis strike Aden airport with two ballistic missiles after an evacuation warning; civilians are injured and air traffic halts. Yemen's army calls it the sixth Houthi strike on the airport in days.36,117

content.intro: This page profiles 45 jihadist groups in four families: who leads each one, where it operates, how the groups link to each other, and what happened in the last 30 days. Hover or tap any marker, node or card for the detail. Superscript numbers open the sources at the bottom. Contested facts carry a confidence level and a reason. Descriptive analysis only.
content.finding: Africa is now the centre of gravity of the movement. Militant Islamist groups caused 23,872 deaths in Africa in the 12 months to mid-2026, 42% of them in the Sahel, and 12 of the 45 groups tracked here are based on the continent.
content.finding_html: Africa is now the centre of gravity of the movement. Militant Islamist groups caused 23,872 deaths in Africa in the 12 months to mid-2026, 42% of them in the Sahel, and 12 of the 45 groups tracked here are based on the continent.8
content.bars_title: Deaths linked to militant Islamist groups in Africa, 12 months to mid-2026

bars.name: Sahel
bars.note: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger. JNIM accounts for 76% of the deaths and the Islamic State Sahel Province for 19% (1,842 deaths).

bars.name: Lake Chad Basin
bars.note: Mainly north-eastern Nigeria. Deaths rose 60% in a year.

bars.name: Somalia
bars.note: Derived: 28% of the 23,872 total. 95% of Somalia's deaths are tied to al-Shabaab.

bars.name: North Africa

takeaway.lead: Africa is the main arena for both al-Qaeda and the Islamic State.
takeaway.html: Africa Center counts 23,872 deaths in Africa in the 12 months to mid-2026, a record, and the UN Monitoring Team describes both movements gaining ground on the continent.8,1

takeaway.lead: JNIM is the largest group in the movement, and it still concedes ground at times.
takeaway.html: It has 7,000 to 8,000 members and keeps Bamako short of fuel, yet Mali's army, backed by Russia's Africa Corps, retook Kidal on 6 October.1,114,10

takeaway.lead: The Islamic State's strength lies in its African provinces, not its core.
takeaway.html: Islamic State West Africa was linked to 3,520 deaths in the past year and the Sahel province to 1,842, while the core lost its deputy leader in May 2026 and keeps up to 3,000 fighters, mostly in Syria.8,1

takeaway.lead: Al-Qaeda's centre is marginal and its energy sits in two affiliates.
takeaway.html: The UN says its senior leadership is marginalised and faces declining relevance. AQAP has about 2,000 fighters and is reported to work with the Houthis, and al-Shabaab trains with the Houthis, as reported.1

takeaway.lead: The Iran-backed axis is fighting on several fronts at once.
takeaway.html: The Houthis hit Riyadh's airport on 10 October, killing 12 people, and struck Aden's airport on 28 October. Israeli strikes continue in southern Lebanon despite the June ceasefire framework. Iraqi factions keep their weapons after US troops left on 1 October, and Hamas has a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, since 20 July.34,36,31,47,42

takeaway.lead: In South Asia the Taliban shelter the Pakistani Taliban and fight the Islamic State.
takeaway.html: The UN reports that the Taliban give the Pakistani Taliban greater freedom of movement, while the Islamic State Khorasan Province is the Taliban's greatest threat, and border clashes with Pakistan continue.1,55

takeaway.lead: Southeast Asia's old groups are gone.
takeaway.html: Jemaah Islamiyah dissolved in June 2024, the East Indonesia Mujahideen is declared eradicated, Abu Sayyaf is under 100 remnants, and the leaders of the Maute group and the BIFF Bungos faction were killed in April and July 2026.63,68,73,71

storylines.bottom: JNIM and the Islamic State Sahel Province fight each other as well as the army.10
Suspected Islamic State West Africa fighters overran an army base, Boko Haram killed farmers and Lakurawa attacked troops in Kebbi.20,62,23
Al-Shabaab ambushed Somali troops while Puntland forces pushed Islamic State Somalia in the Cal Miskaad mountains.13,27
Islamic State-linked fighters keep attacking civilians in Ituri and Cabo Delgado.24,25
Houthi missiles struck the airports of Riyadh and Aden, Israeli strikes continue in southern Lebanon, and Jordan struck alleged Islamic State hideouts in Syria.34,36,31,16
Cross-border and insurgent attacks continue from Pakistan to Iran.55,76
Philippine forces keep killing Dawlah Islamiyah leaders.75

content.confidence_note: Confidence is high when two independent sources agree or the UN Monitoring Team states it, medium when one reliable source reports it, and low when it rests on a single government, group or analyst claim. A link is documented when an official or UN record states it and reported when a news or analyst source says so.
content.gaps: Not yet covered: Ajnad Bayt al-Maqdis, Ansar al-Tawhid, Hizbul Mujahideen, Central Asian groups, Lebanese Sunni groups, other Palestinian factions and Iran's Afghan and Pakistani Shia brigades. No credible strength estimate exists for Hezbollah, al-Shabaab, the Islamic State Khorasan Province, the Pakistani Taliban, Lashkar-e-Taiba, Jaish-e-Mohammed or the Iraqi factions, so none is shown. Map positions are the approximate centre of each group's operating area, not a headquarters.
